source.title: Structural identifiability of partially-observed stochastic processes: from single-particle trajectories to total particle density data

cards.observed_relation: The preprint studies structural identifiability for partially observed stochastic processes and reports different identifiability outcomes when the available data are individual trajectories versus population-level density measurements.
cards.transferable_relation: Identifiability can change when the observation object changes even when the underlying modeled process family is related; the measurement object must therefore be part of an identifiability claim.
admissible_assays: Hold the latent model family fixed while changing only the admitted observation object and report which parameter or route distinctions remain identifiable.
alternative_explanations: Differences may depend on the studied stochastic model, initial conditions, or the mathematical tools available for each observation type rather than a universal partial-observation law.
falsifiers: Changing the admitted observation object leaves the declared identifiability class unchanged across a model family specifically authored to expose observation-dependent distinctions.
forbidden_inferences: Observation-dependent identifiability in a stochastic particle model does not establish TD613 stochastic dynamics or a universal information geometry.

source.title: Disentangling Dynamical Systems: Causal Representation Learning Meets Local Sparse Attention
source.venue: CLeaR / Proceedings of Machine Learning Research

cards.observed_relation: The paper derives an identifiability theorem for system-parameter representations under a declared causal graphical criterion and reports that local state-dependent causal structure can be necessary for stronger disentanglement guarantees.
cards.transferable_relation: Identifiability guarantees belong to an explicit structural assumption set and equivalence class; changing those assumptions can change what unique recovery means.
admissible_assays: State the structural assumptions and allowed equivalence class before testing recovery, then deliberately violate one assumption to locate the guarantee boundary.
alternative_explanations: The particular graphical criterion and learned representation class may not transfer beyond the studied causal-system-identification setting.
falsifiers: A claimed identifiability guarantee survives removal of an assumption that its own theorem requires without a revised proof or weaker equivalence class.
forbidden_inferences: A TD613 representation is not thereby a causal representation or identified physical system parameter.

cards.observed_relation: The paper analyzes intrinsic indeterminacies in latent causal identification and proves identifiability only under stated model and reference-condition assumptions, with partial results when some assumptions are violated.
cards.transferable_relation: A recovery claim must name the transformations or ambiguities under which the latent object is identifiable and retain partial identifiability when assumptions do not support full recovery.
admissible_assays: Report exact recovery, recovery up to declared equivalence, and partial identifiability as separate outcomes rather than collapsing them into one success label.
alternative_explanations: The specific ambiguity classes arise from the paper's latent linear-Gaussian causal model and may differ in other model families.
falsifiers: A method claims unique latent identification while multiple transformations remain observationally equivalent under the declared data and assumptions.
forbidden_inferences: Latent causal identifiability theory does not establish TD613 latent physical variables or causal ontology.

source.title: Nonparametric Partial Disentanglement via Mechanism Sparsity: Sparse Actions, Interventions and Sparse Temporal Dependencies

cards.observed_relation: The paper develops nonparametric identifiability results under mechanism-sparsity assumptions and explicitly distinguishes partial disentanglement up to a declared consistency relation from complete disentanglement under stronger graphical conditions.
cards.transferable_relation: Partial recovery up to a declared equivalence relation is a legitimate identifiability outcome; stronger uniqueness requires stronger assumptions rather than more confident wording.
admissible_assays: When full unique recovery fails, identify the surviving equivalence class and test whether stronger assumptions legitimately shrink that class.
alternative_explanations: Mechanism sparsity is one route to identifiability and need not be the relevant structural assumption in unrelated inverse problems.
falsifiers: A claimed complete-identifiability result cannot distinguish candidate latents that remain equivalent under the declared observation and assumption set.
forbidden_inferences: Partial disentanglement theory does not imply TD613 latent-factor ontology, causal sparsity, or physical structure.
